# ECN-2026-035 Change notice - Machining hydraulic forging press #2

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P1, line P1-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-HP02

## Reason for change
Background: During a recent preventive maintenance review and field inspection of EQ-P1-L3-HP02, an inconsistency in reported ram preload and bolt condition was noted relative to OEM maintenance guidance. The inspection highlighted potential for gradual preload loss at the main ram retention interface that could affect dimensional stability of forged parts and increase wear on mating components. To address this risk and align shop practice with observed field conditions, the bolting requirement for the main ram retention assembly is being formalized and propagated into local procedures.

Root cause rationale: Variability in previous torque application practices, combined with differing interpretations of older documentation, resulted in inconsistent clamping at the main ram. Standardizing the torque to a controlled value reduces variability in clamping force and improves repeatability of ram axial position under load cycles. The controlled torque value complements existing inspection checkpoints and sharpening of procedural references.

Safety and quality drivers: Ensuring consistent clamping at the main ram retention reduces potential for sudden bolt loosening that could compromise operator safety and product dimensional control. This change lowers the likelihood of unplanned disruptions and the need for intrusive corrective maintenance.

Related procedure alignment: The change requires updates and cross-references to local operating procedures SOP-P1-L3-02, SOP-P1-L3-04, and SOP-P1-L3-05 to ensure that operating, maintenance, and inspection teams apply the same requirement and recordkeeping practices.

## Affected items
Scope: This change applies to the main ram retention bolting and associated maintenance and inspection steps on EQ-P1-L3-HP02 located at Plant P1, line P1-L3. Affected documents and records include SOP-P1-L3-02, SOP-P1-L3-04, SOP-P1-L3-05, the PM task list for the press, and the press maintenance log.

Affected personnel: Machining and maintenance technicians who perform torqueing and bolt inspections, shift supervisors who approve maintenance operations, and quality personnel who review process capability records.

Parts and consumables: Existing fasteners used on the main ram retention assembly remain unchanged; however, the approved torque value and the method of application are now mandatory as described in the implementation section.

Performance impact: The change is intended to stabilize ram axial retention and reduce component cyclic fretting. Operators should expect improved dimensional repeatability on forged parts produced by EQ-P1-L3-HP02.

## Implementation
Specified requirement: The main ram bolt torque for Machining hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L3-HP02) is 1330 N·m.

Procedural changes: 
- Update SOP-P1-L3-02 to include a dedicated step for applying and verifying the specified torque during reassembly of the main ram retention. The step must reference the exact applied torque value and specify verification by torque-measuring equipment.
- Update SOP-P1-L3-04 to require a visual and torque-verified check after any operation that requires main ram disassembly or loosening of the retention fasteners. The procedure must require documenting the torque verification result in the equipment maintenance log.
- Update SOP-P1-L3-05 to add an inspection checkpoint during routine press checks that confirms the torque verification entry exists for the most recent maintenance event affecting the main ram retention.

Tooling and measurement: Use calibrated torque application tools capable of applying and recording the specified torque value. Verification may be manual reading from a calibrated torque wrench or electronic capture from a torque tool with data export capability. Calibration status of torque tools must be current and traceable in tool calibration records.

Step-by-step implementation example (high level):
- Prepare press for maintenance following existing lockout procedures as per SOP-P1-L3-04.
- Clean mating surfaces and fastener threads to ensure consistent seating.
- Apply the specified torque to the main ram bolt using an appropriate calibrated torque tool.
- Record the applied torque and tool identifier in the maintenance log entry for the task.
- Perform post-torque inspection for proper seating and absence of thread lubricant contamination that might alter effective torque.
- Resume press operation only after documentation is complete and verified by the shift supervisor.

Training and competency: Technicians assigned to EQ-P1-L3-HP02 must complete a short training brief on the new torque requirement and on proper use of torque-measuring tools. Training records must be retained in the local training file.

Records to keep:
- Maintenance log entries for each main ram retention task that include the applied torque value, technician identifier, torque tool identifier, and calibration sticker/reference.
- Calibration certificates for torque application tools used on EQ-P1-L3-HP02.
- Updated versions of SOP-P1-L3-02, SOP-P1-L3-04, and SOP-P1-L3-05 reflecting the change.
- Training completion records for affected technicians.

Verification and follow-up: Post-implementation monitoring will include review of maintenance log entries and a targeted audit of one maintenance event per shift in the first implementation period to confirm compliance with the specified torque requirement and documentation practice. Findings from these audits will feed back into procedural clarification or retraining as required.

## Approvals
Change prepared by: Maintenance engineering for Plant P1, line P1-L3.

Change reviewed by: Production supervision and quality engineering for the machining line.

Change authorized by: Maintenance manager for Plant P1.

Document control: This ECN is to be filed with the equipment maintenance records and linked to SOP-P1-L3-02, SOP-P1-L3-04, and SOP-P1-L3-05 in the document control system.
